description: Rework the issue detail first screen into an execution control workspace by enriching RuntimeDecisionSurface with decision-adjacent evidence, a compact runner/session signal, and first-screen drift recovery, while demoting descriptive content below the control region.

tasks.title: Decision-adjacent evidence: make plan/check artifacts openable from the control region
tasks.description: Extract the openable-artifact behavior (artifact list rows + selectedArtifactId local state + ArtifactContentViewer modal) from LatestArtifactsPanel into a reusable ArtifactOpener component that both the full panel and a compact decision-context list can compose. Add an optional summary-gated `evidence` slot to RuntimeDecisionSurface that renders the compact ArtifactOpener when the decision summary is approval-required, blocked, or failed. Wire IssueDetailPage to pass the evidence data into the surface so an owner can open plan/check artifacts from the control region without scrolling into reading-flow. The full LatestArtifactsPanel stays in reading-flow for complete browsing; TanStack Query dedupes the shared artifact query key so the two call sites do not double-fetch.
acceptanceCriteria: ArtifactOpener component extracted from LatestArtifactsPanel; LatestArtifactsPanel composes ArtifactOpener and renders byte-for-byte unchanged (same data-testid anchors latest-artifacts-list / latest-artifact-item, same viewer behavior).

RuntimeDecisionSurface accepts an optional `evidence` prop (DecisionEvidence type) and renders the compact artifact list inside the surface section only when decision.summary is approval-required, blocked, or failed.

Clicking a compact artifact item in the surface opens the ArtifactContentViewer modal (same modal as the full panel); the owner does not need to scroll into reading-flow to open artifacts during an approval or recovery decision.
Non-applicable states (running, queued, done) render identically to before — no evidence block appears, no layout shift, existing data-summary/data-tone/data-testid anchors preserved.
IssueDetailPage passes the evidence prop to RuntimeDecisionSurface using data already available (issueNumber, workflowRunId); no new network call beyond the deduped TanStack Query key.

New spec tests cover: artifacts reachable from the control region during an approval decision; artifacts reachable from the control region during a blocked/failed recovery decision; full LatestArtifactsPanel still renders in reading-flow unchanged.
Existing IssueDetailPage test suite passes (status-header, reading-flow, reference-rail tests updated where the new in-surface artifact items affect document-order or cross-tier assertions).
tasks.output: packages/web/src/widgets/issue-workflow/ui/ArtifactOpener.tsx (extracted); RuntimeDecisionSurface.tsx enriched with evidence slot; IssueDetailPage.tsx wired; updated + new spec tests
tasks.notes: Per design D2: the full panel stays in reading-flow; only the openable behavior is shared. Reuse existing latest-artifact-item testid in the compact list so content-viewer tests apply to both call sites. Each ArtifactOpener instance owns its own selectedArtifactId so only one viewer opens at a time.

tasks.title: Compact runner/session execution signal surfaced in the control region
tasks.description: Define an ExecutionSignal type carrying a compact active-session cue (session name + transcript link) and/or a runner-gating reason. Compute it in IssueDetailPage from data the page already holds or can cheaply read: the active coder session for the run and the runner state already feeding decision.waitReason (agentStatus.runnerAvailable, capacity). Add an optional `executionSignal` slot to RuntimeDecisionSurface rendered compactly (one line) when a session is active or the runner gates the current decision. Reuse the runner-gating reason text already produced by buildWaitReason so the compact signal and the existing runtime-wait-reason stay consistent. Omit the signal entirely when no session is active and the runner does not gate a decision.
acceptanceCriteria: ExecutionSignal type defined (active session cue and/or runner-gating reason) and computed in IssueDetailPage — not inside RuntimeDecisionSurface and not by extending RuntimeDecision/deriveRuntimeDecision.

RuntimeDecisionSurface accepts an optional `executionSignal` prop and renders a compact signal (data-testid runtime-execution-signal) inside the section only when a session is active or the runner gates the current decision.
When a workflow run has an active coder session, a compact session signal (session name + transcript link) is visible in the control region without scrolling to the sessions panel.

When no runner is connected or runner capacity is full and the issue cannot start, the runner-gating reason is visible in the control region and matches the text produced by buildWaitReason (consistency with runtime-wait-reason).
When no session is active and the runner does not gate any current decision (backlog, done, normal running), the compact signal is omitted and the surface renders identically to before.
Full WorkflowSessionsPanel remains in reading-flow unchanged.

New spec tests cover: active session shows compact signal in control region; runner unavailable surfaced in control region; capacity-full surfaced in control region; signal omitted when not decision-relevant.
Existing IssueDetailPage test suite passes (capacity-gating test consistency maintained; no regression on queued/backlog/done paths).
tasks.output: ExecutionSignal type; IssueDetailPage.tsx computes and passes executionSignal; RuntimeDecisionSurface.tsx enriched with executionSignal slot; new spec tests
tasks.notes: Per design D3: the page is the data owner (matches the existing pattern where the page computes decision and passes it down). Do NOT extend RuntimeDecision or deriveRuntimeDecision with session detail — that mixes adjudication with execution-plane evidence and violates the consumed-unchanged constraint.

tasks.title: First-screen drift recovery entry point with shared rebase hook
tasks.description: Extract the rebase-recovery trigger (mutation + useWorkspaceStatus read + useLiveTask conflict state + rebaseQueued local state + pending/error handling) from BranchBar into a small reusable hook/handler so both the surface's drift slot and BranchBar share one implementation. Add an optional `driftRecovery` slot to RuntimeDecisionSurface rendered as a compact drift-recovery block carrying the rebase action when issue.drift.drifted is true and the drift decision needs attention (the condition that already sets decision.driftNote). Wire IssueDetailPage to compute the DriftRecoveryAction and pass it to the surface. The reference-rail IssueDriftCard remains unchanged for full drift detail (base SHA, defer reason, conflicts); the first-screen entry promotes the action, not the detail. BranchBar stays in reading-flow for ongoing branch-status display.
acceptanceCriteria: Rebase-recovery hook/handler extracted from BranchBar; BranchBar composes the shared hook and its rebase behavior (mutation, workspace-status invalidation, conflict/queued/pending states, error rendering) is unchanged.

RuntimeDecisionSurface accepts an optional `driftRecovery` prop (DriftRecoveryAction type) and renders a compact drift-recovery block (data-testid runtime-drift-recovery) inside the section only when drift needs attention and blocks progress.

When an issue has base drift whose decision needs attention (needs-attention) and rebase is the relevant recovery action, the drift signal and rebase action are reachable from the control region without expanding a collapsed reference-rail card.
Triggering rebase from the surface's drift slot uses the same mutation path as BranchBar (shared hook); pending/conflict/error states render consistently between the two call sites.
The reference-rail IssueDriftCard remains available with full drift detail (base SHA, defer reason, conflicts) — the first-screen entry does not replace the rail card.
No new RuntimeActionKind is added (rebase is not added to the action set); rebase flows through its own drift-recovery slot, not through the surface action buttons.
New spec tests cover: drift recovery reachable on first screen when drift blocks progress; reference rail retains full drift detail; BranchBar rebase behavior unchanged after hook extraction.
Blocked and interrupted states still expose their recovery actions (retry/resume/rerun/stop) through the existing surface action buttons — no regression.
tasks.output: Shared rebase-recovery hook; RuntimeDecisionSurface.tsx enriched with driftRecovery slot; IssueDetailPage.tsx wired; BranchBar.tsx refactored to use shared hook; new spec tests
tasks.notes: Per design D4: rebase is a branch operation, not a workflow lifecycle action — it must NOT be added to RuntimeActionKind or the backend allowedActions set. The surface promotes the rebase ACTION for the decision moment; BranchBar retains ongoing branch status. Shared rebase hook prevents logic drift between the two call sites.

tasks.title: Control workspace composition, content demotion, and cross-cutting spec verification
tasks.description: After all three slots are wired, verify and adjust the page-level first-screen hierarchy so the control region is a coherent execution control workspace across every conditional path. Confirm description, comments, model selection, and prerequisites reside below the control region and no new operational content leaked above them. Assert the tier-weight invariants (data-tier-weight containers, single-sticky StatusHeadline, lg:col-span-2/col-span-1 ratio) and every existing data-testid anchor hold under the new composition. Add the cross-cutting spec test suite covering all conditional paths (running, approval-required, blocked, interrupted, drift, failed, queued/backlog, done, archived) against the full control workspace contract, and verify every existing lifecycle action and its gating is preserved with no new workflow actions introduced.
acceptanceCriteria: First-screen control region shows issue identity, adjudicated workflow status summary, stage/progress, approval state, primary owner action, and (when relevant) the evidence/signal/drift slots — all within the status-header tier preceding reading-flow and reference-rail, reachable without scrolling on every conditional path.

Description and comments appear in the reading-flow tier below the operational content in document order; model selection and prerequisites remain in the reference-rail configuration card; none appear within the first-screen control region.

Backlog issue shows identity and queued/backlog situation without fabricated stage, progress figure, or runtime action; done/archived issue shows terminal state with no start/stop/approve/retry/resume/rerun action offered.

Tier-weight invariants hold: three data-tier-weight containers, single-sticky StatusHeadline, lg:col-span-2/col-span-1 ratio, every block in exactly one tier — verified across all conditional paths including the new in-surface slots.
All existing data-testid anchors preserved; new anchors (runtime-evidence, runtime-execution-signal, runtime-drift-recovery) are additive and follow the runtime-* naming convention.

Every existing lifecycle action (start, approve, send-back, retry, resume, rerun, stop/force-stop, rebase, close, archive, mark-ready) remains available in its valid context with gating matching the pre-existing backend projection; no action outside the existing set is offered.
Disabled/unsafe actions are visually secondary (disabled or secondary weight); the primary valid action carries default-variant emphasis; stop still requires confirmation within the control region.
Existing IssueDetailPage.*.test.tsx suite (status-header, reading-flow, reference-rail, capacity-gating, archived, cross-tier, narrow-action-bar, readiness) updated for the new hierarchy and passing.

New cross-cutting spec tests cover: running/approval/blocked/interrupted/drift/failed/queued/done/archived paths against the control workspace contract; secondary-content demotion; lifecycle action preservation; no-new-actions invariant.
tasks.output: IssueDetailPage.tsx composition adjustments (if any); updated IssueDetailPage.*.test.tsx suite; new cross-cutting spec test file(s) covering the full control workspace contract
tasks.notes: Per design D5: demotion is structural, not deletion. The three data-tier-weight containers, single-sticky StatusHeadline, spacing scale, and cross-tier audit are preserved. This task is the integration verification point — it validates that the three slot features compose into a coherent control workspace and that no regression escaped the per-feature tests. Assert every conditional path per the risk mitigation in design Risks/Trade-offs.
